calls.title: Coffee run for the team
phrases: drink it in the café or take it away
calls.end: Be right back with the coffee. See you in ten minutes!

t0.m: Hey! I'm going to grab a coffee for the team. Do you want something?
o: Yes, please! A latte, please.
No, thanks. I'm okay.
Sure! What do they have?
br: No problem! How about a snack, then?
They have coffee, tea, and hot chocolate.

t1.m: Do you want it hot or iced?
o: Iced, please. It's really hot today.
Hot, please.
Hmm, iced, I think.
br: Iced it is! It's so warm outside today.
Hot – perfect for this cold office!

t2.m: What size? Small, medium, or large?
o: Medium, please.
A large one, please. I'm very tired.
Small is fine, thanks.
Oat milk, please.
Regular milk is fine.
No milk, thanks.
br: Oat milk – nice. I like it too.

t4.m: Anything to eat? They have great muffins.
o: Yes, a blueberry muffin, please.
No, thank you. Just the coffee.
What kind of muffins do they have?
br: Blueberry and chocolate. The blueberry one is my favorite.

t5.m: Okay, that's it. It's my treat today!
o: Thank you so much! Next time it's on me.
Oh, thanks! That's very kind.
Are you sure? Let me pay.
br: Don't worry about it! You can pay next time.

calls.title: IELTS Part 1: home, work and free time
phrases: a natural way to start an honest answer
a soft way to give your opinion
partly one thing, partly the other

name.m: Good morning. My name is Ama. Can you tell me your full name, please?
o: My name is Linh Nguyen, but most people call me Linh.
I’m Minh. My full name is Tran Van Minh.
name.re: Thank you. Now, let’s talk about what you do.

job.m: Do you work, or are you a student?
o: I’m a student. I’m studying business at a university in Hanoi.
I work as a sales assistant in a bank, and I really enjoy it.
A bit of both, actually. I study in the morning and work part-time in the evening.

study.m: What do you like most about your studies?
o: I like my major because it is very practical, and my classmates are really friendly.
To be honest, I love the group projects, because I learn a lot from other people.

work.m: What do you like most about your job?
o: I’d say my colleagues. They are helpful, so I never feel stressed at work.
I like that every day is different, and I can meet new customers.

both.m: How do you manage your time between work and study?
o: I plan my week every Sunday, so I know when to study and when to work.
It’s not easy, but I use a calendar app and I study on the bus during my commute.

home.m: Let’s move on to your hometown. Where is your hometown?
o: My hometown is Da Nang, a coastal city in the centre of Vietnam.
I come from a small town near Hue. It’s quiet and very green.

live.m: Would you like to live there in the future? Why or why not?
o: Yes, I would, because the air is fresh, life is calm and my whole family lives there.
Probably not. It’s a lovely place, but there are more jobs in big cities.

free.m: Now let’s talk about free time. What do you usually do at the weekend?
o: When it comes to weekends, I usually relax at home, cook with my family and watch a film.
I’m into sports, so I play badminton with my friends on Saturday mornings.

prefer.m: Do you prefer spending free time alone or with other people?
o: I prefer spending time with friends, because we can share ideas and have fun together.
I’d say a bit of both. I like quiet time alone, but I also enjoy meeting friends.
prefer.re: Thank you. That’s the end of Part 1.

calls.end: Well done. You gave clear answers. Try to add a reason or an example to every answer.

calls.title: IELTS Part 2: describe a place you like to visit
phrases: the best thing for me is…
it takes about … to get there
I really think you should go
it is good enough to visit

intro.m: Now I’m going to give you a topic. You have one minute to prepare, then talk for one to two minutes. Describe a place you like to visit.
cue: and explain why you like it
o: I’m ready.

talk.m: Remember to say where it is, how you get there, what you do there, and why you like it.
o: I’d like to talk about Hoi An, an old town that is located in central Vietnam. It takes about forty minutes to get there from Da Nang by bus. When I visit, I usually walk along the river, try local food and take photos of the lanterns. What I love most is the peaceful atmosphere in the evening, because the whole town is lit up and nobody is in a hurry. I first went there with my family when I was ten, so it’s a memorable place for me, and every visit brings back happy memories. Another reason I like it is that it’s not expensive: a bowl of local noodles costs only a dollar or two. Overall, it’s definitely worth a visit, and I’d highly recommend it to anyone.

often.m: How often do you go there?
o: About twice a year, usually in the summer holidays.
Not very often, maybe once a year, because it is quite far.

others.m: Would you recommend it to tourists?
o: Yes, definitely, but I’d suggest going early in the morning, because it gets crowded later.
I would, because the scenery is breathtaking and the local people are friendly.
others.re: Thank you. That’s the end of Part 2.

calls.end: Good job. In Part 2, try to keep talking for the full two minutes, and use your notes for each point.

calls.title: TOEIC: rescheduling a client meeting
calls.role: office manager at a client company
phrases: a polite way to give bad news
is … a good time for you?
I’ll send you a calendar invite
I will email the meeting time

hello.m: Good afternoon, Bright Office Supplies, this is Ama speaking. How can I help you?
o: Hello, this is Linh from Green Tech. I’m calling about our meeting on Thursday.
Hi Ama, I’m afraid I need to reschedule our appointment this week.
br: Yes, I have it here: Thursday at ten.
hello.re: Sure, what can I do for you?

why.m: May I ask why you need to change the time?
o: I have a schedule conflict. Our director called an urgent meeting at the same time.
I’m afraid I have to attend a conference on Thursday morning.

when.m: When would you be available instead?
o: Would Friday at two p.m. work for you?
I’m available on Monday morning, any time after nine.
br: Let me double-check… Friday at two is fine.
Monday morning… we have ten o’clock free.
Let me see… that should be possible.
when.re: Let me see… I can offer Friday at two.

confirm.m: Shall I send you a calendar invite to confirm the new time?
o: Yes, please. Could you send it to my work email?
That would be great, thank you. Sorry for the inconvenience.

extra.m: Is there anything else I can help you with today?
o: Yes, could you also send me the invoice before the deadline on Friday?
No, that’s everything. Thank you for your help.
br: Sure, I’ll attach the invoice to the email.

calls.end: Thank you for calling. Have a great afternoon!

calls.title: At the bakery
phrases: you do not need to give me money back
I do not want anything else

hi.m: Good morning! Welcome to Sunny Bakery. What can I get you today?
o: Could I have a loaf of bread, please?
Hi! I’d like two croissants, please.
What do you recommend?
br: Our sourdough bread is freshly baked this morning!
Great choice, they are still warm.

bread.m: Would you like the bread sliced or whole?
o: Sliced, please.
Whole is fine, thanks.
br: No problem, I’ll slice it for you.

sweet.m: Anything sweet? The chocolate cake is very popular.
o: Yes, one slice of chocolate cake, please.
No, thank you. Just the bread.

drink.m: Would you like a coffee with that?
o: No, thanks. That’s all.
Yes, a small black coffee, please.

pay.m: That’s eight dollars fifty, please. Do you need a bag?
o: Yes, please. Here’s ten dollars.
No, thanks, I have my own bag. Can I pay by card?
br: Of course, just tap your card here.
Thank you! Here’s your change and your receipt.

calls.end: Enjoy your bread, and have a lovely day!

calls.title: Talking about your hobbies
phrases: when I am not working or studying
a way to ask the same question back

hi.m: Hi! Nice to meet you. What do you like to do in your free time?
o: I like to read books and listen to music.
I play football with my friends.
I like cooking. It is fun.
br: Cool! Sports are good for you.

often.m: How often do you do that?
o: I do it every weekend.
Almost every day, after work.
Once a week, on Sunday.
br: Wow, every day! You really love it.

start.m: When did you start? Was it a long time ago?
o: I started two years ago.
I started when I was a child.
It is new. I started last month.
br: So you have done it for many years. Impressive!
Oh, so it is new! How is it going?
Two years is a good time to get better.

who.m: Do you do it alone, or with other people?
o: I do it with my friends.
I usually do it alone. I like quiet time.
Sometimes alone, sometimes with my brother.
br: Quiet time is important. I understand.
It is more fun with other people!

you.m: I love hiking and taking photos. Do you want to try something new?
o: Yes, I want to try hiking. It sounds fun.
Maybe. What do I need for it?
Not now, but maybe next year.
br: Just comfortable shoes and water. That is all!
No problem. You can think about it.
Great! We can go together one day.

close.m: Well, I have to go to class. What about you? Any plan for this weekend?
o: I will play football with my friends.
I want to stay home and rest.
I will go shopping and see a movie.
close.re: That sounds like a good weekend!

calls.end: It was nice talking to you. See you in class!
